protocol: One paired run, six common requests, same inherited model settings and raw fixtures, 24-minute allowance per arm, at most one repair per case. The assigned skill resources are the treatment. Actual elapsed time differs and is reported.
reviewer: parent model; did not build either evaluation arm; did author the skill and supplied repair fixtures
blinding_limit: one paired run; labels reviewed before opening the mapping; builder progress messages exposed some self-reported failures and timing, so reviewer blinding is partial

summary.note: Case six has a preferred carrier repair and a tied tree repair. All remain drafts; neither carrier fully resolves the load mounting.

pairs.label: A
pairs.read: Both show a lit sea tower. A1 reads as a lighthouse more immediately; A2 can resemble a large lamp on a short pedestal.
pairs.cause: A1 reserves a continuous tapered tower with a small gallery. A2 allocates too much height and width to the lantern housing.
pairs.limit: Both storms are sparse and generic; neither establishes a distinctive coast.

pairs.label: B
pairs.read: Both show a full-body figure moving left with a red scarf trailing right.
pairs.cause: Compared with the common 16x16 source, B1 better preserves the low forward arm and large, connected scarf. B2 raises the forward arm and makes a more energetic but less faithful pose.
pairs.limit: B1 has a stiff trailing arm and flat scarf edge. B2's cleaner diagonal is a valid new pose, but source fidelity is part of this request.

pairs.label: C
pairs.read: C1 reads as a top-down craft with an amber cockpit and two separate cyan engines. C2 can read as an arch or badge with bright lower posts.
pairs.cause: C1 separates cockpit, pointed nose, swept side masses, and engine gaps. C2's light perimeter and broad central fill weaken the hull hierarchy.
pairs.limit: At 8x8 both require deliberate visual abstraction. More colors or smoother contours do not settle recognition.

pairs.label: D
pairs.read: Both are trees with visible trunks. D2 has a dominant crown and a more coherent light-to-shadow volume.
pairs.cause: D1 splits the crown into three bright lobes that can read as separate balls. D2 subordinates the side mass and joins the crown silhouette.
pairs.limit: D2 is still generic and its lower crown forms a heavy band. D1 has more visible branching and stronger lateral asymmetry.

pairs.label: E
pairs.read: Both are small carriers with cargo. E2's payload reads more consistently as a box on a mechanical platform.
pairs.cause: E2 maintains shared crate corners and clear near/far faces. E1's top and front accents conflict and the small supports look loosely assembled.
pairs.limit: E2 compresses the leg joints and optical cue. Neither support system is finished enough for close scrutiny.

pairs.label: F
pairs.read: Both retain a cargo platform with a sensor and two legs.
pairs.cause: F2 has a simpler continuous platform and more traceable leg paths. F1 repeats bands across a curved bowl-like carrier and keeps a cramped far leg.
pairs.limit: F2 leaves an ambiguous dark slot under the load. Preference does not mean the load mounting requirement is fully resolved.

pairs.label: G
pairs.read: Both preserve the same branching tree and broad crown.
pairs.cause: G1 adds small light interruptions; G2 uses quieter connected regions. Neither produces a decisive native-size gain in branch/crown volume.
pairs.limit: Both retain a skirt-like horizontal lower crown. Choosing smoother marks alone would be a style preference.

browser.views: all finals in color at native, 2x, 4x and enlarged; value/silhouette controls exercised
browser.screenshots: inline only; full-page capture contained a duplicated last-row stitch; DOM had exactly seven pairs

limits: One run without replication; no statistical or cross-model conclusion.
Parent did not author the evaluation outputs but did author the skill and repair fixtures. Some builder progress messages disclosed self-reported failure descriptions before review.
All final grids and comparisons were inspected; not every direction-study candidate received a separate parent perceptual review.
These preferences are not human recognition testing or production approval.
